issues.claim: the March 2026 DHS appropriations lapse likely pushing the timeline further
issues.issue: The DHS appropriations lapse began on February 14, 2026, not in March 2026. The phrasing 'the March 2026 DHS appropriations lapse' mischaracterizes when the lapse started. While the lapse was ongoing during March (when it affected the CIRCIA town halls), calling it a 'March 2026' lapse is inaccurate. Multiple sources (CNN, Wikipedia, Envoy Global) confirm the DHS partial shutdown began February 14, 2026 after DHS funding expired on February 13.
issues.suggested_fix: Change 'the March 2026 DHS appropriations lapse' to 'the DHS appropriations lapse that began in February 2026' or 'the ongoing DHS appropriations lapse'.

issues.claim: a lapse in DHS appropriations in March 2026 forced CISA to cancel all scheduled town halls
issues.section: Town Hall Meetings and DHS Shutdown
issues.issue: Same issue as above: the DHS appropriations lapse began February 14, 2026, not 'in March 2026'. The cancellations were announced in March because the town halls were scheduled to start March 9, but the underlying lapse began in February. The phrase 'in March 2026' implies the lapse started in March.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to 'the ongoing lapse in DHS appropriations (which began February 14, 2026) forced CISA to cancel all scheduled town halls' or similar phrasing that correctly identifies the lapse start date.
